_note: Register fragment for the published-service-and-case-type-catalogue change (ADR-037). Four schemas: the public request catalogue entry, the published case type definition, the knowledge article and the reader's verdict on it. The verdict is a separate object so a reader token never lands on the article an anonymous reader can read.

serviceCatalogueEntry.comment: Read on every public catalogue request, so it gets a dedicated SQL table

caseTypeDefinition.comment: Published case type, imported from or synchronised with an external case type catalogue

knowledgeArticle.comment: A knowledge article is a published record, governed by the publication rules

articleVerdict.comment: One verdict per reader token per article; never read by an anonymous reader

serviceCatalogueEntry.title: Service catalogue entry
serviceCatalogueEntry.summary: One service a resident or a company can request
serviceCatalogueEntry.description: An entry in the public request catalogue. It names what the requester gets, what it costs in money and in time, and carries the form binding that starts it. The entry never holds the form itself: the portal resolves the binding and renders.

title.title: Title
title.description: What the requester asks for, in their words.

group.title: Group
group.description: The grouping the catalogue lists this entry under.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.description: The catalogue this entry is published in.

amount.description: The amount, in the given currency.

description.description: The cost in words, for a cost that is not a single amount.

unit.description: The unit the term is counted in.

formBinding.title: Form binding
formBinding.description: What the portal needs to render the form that starts this. The catalogue holds no field list.

caseType.description: The case type the request opens.

audience.description: The audience the form is rendered for.

formName.description: The name of the form in the portal.

caseTypeDefinition.title: Case type definition
caseTypeDefinition.summary: A case type published with its form and its API description
caseTypeDefinition.description: A case type definition published in a catalogue. It links to the form that starts it and to the API description of the interface behind it. When it came from an external catalogue it also carries where it came from, at what version, when it was imported, and the values it held at that moment, which is what a resynchronisation is compared against.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: The case type identifier, unique within its source.

formUrl.title: Form URL
formUrl.description: The form that starts a case of this type.

apiDescriptionUrl.title: API description URL
apiDescriptionUrl.description: The OpenAPI description of the interface behind this type.

publicationText.title: Publication text
publicationText.description: The text published with a record of this type.

inspectionTermDays.title: Inspection term in days
inspectionTermDays.description: The statutory period a record of this type lies open for inspection.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where this definition came from, if it was imported.

externalId.description: The identifier of the definition at the source.

importedSnapshot.title: Imported snapshot
importedSnapshot.description: The values as they arrived. A property that differs from this snapshot was changed locally, and a resynchronisation flags it.

knowledgeArticle.title: Knowledge article
knowledgeArticle.summary: An answer written once, published beside the catalogue
knowledgeArticle.description: A knowledge article is a published record in a catalogue, searchable and public by the rules that govern publications. A draft extracted from a case answer is not public until it is published.

draft.title: Draft
draft.description: A draft is readable by staff only.

sourceCase.title: Source case
sourceCase.description: The case whose answer this article was extracted from.

articleVerdict.title: Article verdict
articleVerdict.summary: One reader's verdict on one article
articleVerdict.description: Whether an article helped one reader. The reader is held as a salted hash of their token, so the article can be counted without the reader being identifiable from it.

article.title: Article
article.description: The article this verdict is on.

readerHash.title: Reader hash
readerHash.description: A salted hash of the reader token. Never the token.
